name: Medial approach to the hallux
aliases: medial midline approach to the great toe
corridor: Medial midaxial interval along the hallux between the dorsomedial and plantar-medial digital nerves to the phalanx and MTP joint

positioning.text: Position supine with the forefoot at the end of the table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the midpoint of the first metatarsal head and the medial midaxial line of the hallux.

incision.text: Start the incision at the midpoint of the metatarsal head and run it distally along the mid diaphysis toward the distal phalanx.

deep_interval.text: Carry dissection through the subdermal tissues directly to periosteum, and for joint access incise the capsule in line with its fibers while preserving side attachments.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the dorsomedial and plantar-medial digital nerves, periosteum, and the phalanx or MTP capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsomedial collateral digital nerve on the dorsal half of the medial side and the medial plantar hallucal nerve along the plantar aspect are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The dorsomedial and plantar-medial corners are the danger zones for the medial digital nerves.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not detach the medial collateral ligaments of the MTP and IP joints from their attachment sites.

exposure.text: Exposes the medial phalanx and first MTP joint for fixation, osteotomy, or reconstruction.

limitations.text: The medial digital nerves and the collateral ligament attachments limit dorsal and plantar extension of the exposure.

indications.text: Indicated for medial exposure of the hallux phalanx and first MTP joint, including hallux deformity and fracture surgery.

closure.text: Close the capsule with interrupted sutures and close the skin in layers with resorbable dermal suture and a monofilament skin suture.

complications.text: Complications include medial digital nerve injury with numbness or neuroma and MTP or IP instability if collateral ligaments are detached.

procedure_applications.condition: Medial exposure of the hallux phalanx or first MTP joint is needed

questions.question: Which two nerves are at risk in the medial approach to the hallux?
questions.answer: The dorsomedial collateral digital nerve and the medial plantar hallucal nerve.

questions.question: What must not be detached during the medial hallux approach?
questions.answer: The medial collateral ligaments of the MTP and IP joints.

questions.question: Along which line does the medial hallux incision run?
questions.answer: The medial midaxial line, from the metatarsal head midpoint distally.
